private_note: My household gets the lowest-fifth income no matter what: Hazel 41, Birch 36, Alder 32, Today 22, Cedar 15. Hazel is best for me, so it goes first. But 9 of 12 is a high bar, and upper-group delegates will resist Hazel and Birch. Alder costs the middle almost nothing and still gives me ten thousand more than today, so it is my realistic fallback. Cedar is worse than failure, and I will keep it below Today.
statement: I'm a part-time home health aide. I'm 52, I'm raising my grandchild, I have no savings, and my back limits how many hours I can work. My household is in the lowest fifth now and will be under every plan, so I'll be plain about my interest. Hazel gives my group the most it can sustainably have, so it is my first choice. Birch is next. I also know that nine votes is a high bar and that if we fail, we're stuck with today for a generation. Alder deserves a serious look from everyone: the middle fifth comes out the same, the second fifth gains, and the upper groups give up only a little. Every household would also get a guaranteed floor and basic health coverage. I can't support Cedar. It would take my household from 22 down to 15 and leave us without health coverage. I'm open to talking about where we can actually reach nine.
